name: Rwanda
status: Seed collections of 19 November 2026: 99 records (rivers, wetlands, lakeshores and land sand pits); daily collector configured in watches/rwanda/collector.json.
scope: Construction-sand extraction and mining in Rwanda from rivers, wetlands and lakeshores and from land and hillside sand pits, with its licensing, cooperatives, enforcement, accidents and deaths in sand pits, livelihoods, prices and supply, construction demand and effects on riverbanks, wetlands, water quality and sedimentation. Each record states whether the site is a river, wetland, lakeshore or land pit. Exclude 3T/gold mineral mining unless the record concerns construction sand, stone quarries without sand, and Lake Kivu methane.
basinAssignment: Assign a record by its named river; Lake Kivu and its tributaries go to the Congo basin. If only a district is named, use the basin holding most of that district and record the assumption in limitations.

sources.name: Rwanda Mines, Petroleum and Gas Board
Research (Google Scholar, University of Rwanda repository, African Journals Online)

editorialNotes: Follow the Bangladesh Sand Watch editorial policy: read the original body, quote date and figures verbatim, attribute allegations, keep district/sector/cell and named river or wetland.
Kinyarwanda headlines and summaries require native-language review before acceptance; keep the original title.
Licences and bans are often reported as announcements; record who announced what and when, without inferring enforcement.
Distinguish tonnes, cubic metres, truckloads and RWF amounts with their time basis.
firstMilestones: Historical backfill of The New Times, KT Press and Kigali Today 2015–2026 for the Nyabarongo, Akanyaru and Sebeya.
Official baseline: RMB licensing notices, REMA and RWB riparian buffer guidance.
Daily collector with Kinyarwanda search terms, writing global-v1 records to watches/rwanda/archive.json in this repository.
